summary: Wilson County, TN: a 1965 federal survey note shows a lookout tower under construction on the knob; Tennessee Landforms lists it standing; no staffing or access details found.

visit.trail_note: Tennessee Landforms advises against climbing these towers because steps are often removed or rotten; we found no public visiting arrangement

events.note: Construction under way in 1965, per the Coast and Geodetic Survey recovery note, which says the survey station had to be lowered for grading. No completion or build date is given.

evidence.supports: elevation about 1,221 feet, Wilson County, standing
Tennessee Landforms advises against climbing; steps often removed or rotten
evidence.quote: You are advised not to climb the towers, often steps have been removed or are rotten.

evidence.supports: many towers removed and most locations now private property
evidence.quote: Many have been removed, and most locations are now private property

evidence.supports: Jennings Knob listed among the Division of Forestry towers, Wilson County
the survey recovery note is from the Coast and Geodetic Survey, 1965

evidence.supports: construction of a forest lookout tower on the site in 1965

corrections.why: NGS is the National Geodetic Survey. GC2150 is a survey mark on the knob, not a lookout register. The cached NHLR Tennessee list does not include Jennings Knob.

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975
sources.publisher: National Park Service (National Register multiple property documentation form)

notes_for_editor: No build year is recorded. The 1965 survey note shows construction under way but gives no completion date. A search snippet from Wikimapia calls the tower an old Division of Forestry fire tower and gives tower number 6-3, but that page did not fetch, so it is not cited; check it before publishing. The record's registers field (NGS None) is proposed for removal under corrections. No staffing, design or access sources were found. Status standing rests on one undated Tennessee Landforms list. Two WebSearch calls were used.
